principles.text: Use the index as support for individual breakouts: if the QQQ is finding support and breaking out intraday, single-stock breakouts have a higher success rate.

Anchor VWAP from three places - the height of the whole base, the recent base's swing high, and the recent swing low; an entry where price reclaims multiple anchored-VWAPs at once is a layered, high-confluence support.
Sell more aggressively into strength in the late stage of an uptrend; hold longer and trim less in the early stage (where he believes the market currently is).
Risk management is the holy grail; keeping losses small and controlling drawdown keeps you in the game long enough to learn and improve, whatever your style or instrument.

Review both your winners and losers - on winners study what you did well (entry/exit/stock pick), on losers whether you entered at the wrong time, exited too early, or mis-set the stop; judge a trade by whether price moved your way after entry and against you after exit.
Build leverage by managing each trade individually and stacking entries over days (3-4 Thursday, 2-3 Friday, 2 Monday) so profit cushions and drawdown control accumulate gradually - not all at once.
Stop copying other traders' rules once past the beginner stage; filter out what does not fit you (drawdown tolerance, win-rate comfort, stop width) and build your own style.
Respect the market most when it is doing well - a hyperbolic equity curve to new all-time highs is the danger lying beneath the surface (the path to euphoria and blow-up).
